nodes.description: Downstream of granule polarization and docking, the SNARE/priming machinery (Munc13-4, syntaxin-11, Munc18-2, RAB27A) is required to fuse perforin- and granzyme-laden lytic granules with the plasma membrane at the immunological synapse. Mutations in these genes block the late exocytosis step even when granules are correctly polarized and docked.

evidence.reference_title: Munc13-4 is essential for cytolytic granules fusion and is mutated in a form of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL3).
evidence.snippet: This process requires the rapid transfer of perforin containing lytic granules to the target cell interface, followed by their docking and fusion with the plasma membrane.

evidence.reference_title: Linkage of familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) type-4 to chromosome 6q24 and identification of mutations in syntaxin 11.
evidence.snippet: As both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, we conclude that, besides mutations in perforin 1, defects in the endocytotic or the exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL.

evidence.reference_title: Munc18-2 deficiency causes familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis type 5 and impairs cytotoxic granule exocytosis in patient NK cells.
evidence.snippet: NK cells exhibited impaired cytotoxic granule exocytosis, a defect that could be overcome by ectopic expression of wild-type STXBP2

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in RAB27A cause Griscelli syndrome associated with haemophagocytic syndrome.
evidence.snippet: RAB27A-deficient T cells exhibited reduced cytotoxicity and cytolytic granule exocytosis, whereas MYO5A-defective T cells did not.

nodes.description: XIAP restrains activation-induced lymphocyte apoptosis, and XIAP-deficient lymphocytes die more readily in response to several activating and death-receptor stimuli. This lesion is XIAP-specific: SAP deficiency shares the NKT-cell deficit but not the apoptotic phenotype, which is why this node carries only XIAP.

evidence.reference_title: XIAP deficiency in humans causes an X-linked lymphoproliferative syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We show that apoptosis of lymphocytes from XIAP-deficient patients is enhanced in response to various stimuli including the T-cell antigen receptor (TCR)-CD3 complex, the death receptor CD95 (also termed Fas or Apo-1) and the TNF-associated apoptosis-inducing ligand receptor (TRAIL-R).

evidence.snippet: Most patients also develop an uncontrolled T-lymphocyte and macrophage activation syndrome (known as haemophagocytic syndrome, HS), leading to death in the absence of bone-marrow transplantation.

nodes.description: The unifying lesion in familial HLH is defective perforin/granzyme-mediated killing by cytotoxic T lymphocytes and NK cells. Loss of perforin (PRF1) or of the granule docking/priming/fusion machinery (Munc13-4, syntaxin-11, Munc18-2, RAB27A) prevents target-cell lysis, so infected and antigen-presenting cells are not eliminated and the immune response cannot be terminated.

evidence.snippet: Cultured lymphocytes from patients had defective cytotoxic activity, and immunostaining revealed little or no perforin in the granules.

nodes.description: Loss of LYST, which regulates membrane dynamics and intracellular trafficking of lysosomes and lysosome-related organelles, leaves those organelles unresolved as giant inclusion bodies with cargo mis-sorted into them. The same machinery failure gives defective granule exocytosis and defective cytotoxicity, which is how Chediak-Higashi syndrome reaches the cytotoxicity lesion the familial HLH genes reach by a different route.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and mutation analysis of the complete gene for Chediak-Higashi syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The CHS hallmark is the occurrence of giant inclusion bodies and organelles in a variety of cell types, and protein sorting defects into these organelles.

evidence.reference_title: Identification and mutation analysis of the complete gene for Chediak-Higashi syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the CHS polypeptide demonstrates that its modular architecture is similar to the yeast vacuolar sorting protein, VPS15.

evidence.reference_title: The lysosomal trafficking regulator "LYST": an 80-year traffic jam.
evidence.snippet: The lysosomal trafficking regulator (LYST) is an elusive protein important for the regulation of membrane dynamics and intracellular trafficking of lysosomes and LROs.

nodes.description: SAP (SH2D1A) and XIAP are both required for the natural killer T-cell compartment, so loss of either depletes NKT cells. In SAP deficiency (XLP1) the depleted compartment accompanies an inappropriate response to Epstein-Barr virus; XIAP deficiency (XLP2) shares the NKT deficit but its hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is often not EBV-triggered, as the XLP2 subtype row of this entry records. This is why the two X-linked genes are wired here rather than to the cytotoxic granule nodes of the entry.

evidence.snippet: We also found that XIAP-deficient patients, like SAP-deficient patients, have low numbers of natural killer T-lymphocytes (NKT cells), indicating that XIAP is required for the survival and/or differentiation of NKT cells.

nodes.description: Because cytotoxic lymphocytes cannot kill the antigen-presenting targets that sustain them, the immune response is never contracted. CTLs and macrophages remain hyperactivated and proliferate, secreting a storm of inflammatory cytokines (notably interferon-gamma), which drives macrophage activation, hemophagocytosis, and multi-organ infiltration and damage (bone marrow, liver, spleen, brain).
